out.other_title: Process supervision (step-level feedback) outperforms outcome supervision on MATH
out.rationale: Sun et al. find that weighted voting outshines Best-of-n, which they say diverges from past research [40, 74] that observed minimal performance differences between the two, and hypothesise that the discrepancy arises from training a less powerful base model (Llemma) on more difficult tasks (MATH), which might diminish the effectiveness of the reward model. Lightman et al. report that process supervision significantly outperforms outcome supervision for training models to solve problems from the MATH dataset, and release the step-level labels used to train their best reward model. The cited Sun et al. passage does not name Lightman et al., and the cited Lightman et al. passage does not address weighted voting, so the weighted-voting finding does not bear on the process-versus-outcome claim and that claim does not bear on the weighted-voting finding; the link proposes only SHARES_TOPIC. No atlas record covers the weighted-voting comparison, so the paper-level record is used; the target is the cited paper's main record, not a record of the specific result.
out.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: Reward models for solving problems from the MATH dataset; the source compares weighted voting with best-of-n for a less powerful base model (Llemma) trained on more difficult tasks (MATH), and the target compares process with outcome supervision

text: The authors find that weighted voting outshines best-of-n reranking, and say this diverges from past research [40, 74], where minimal performance differences were observed between the two. They hypothesize that the discrepancy arises from their specific experiment, which trains a less powerful base model (Llemma) on more difficult tasks (MATH), a setup that might diminish the effectiveness of the reward model and potentially lead to over-optimization of rewards.
title: Weighted voting outshines best-of-n, diverging from past research [40, 74]
